pr_body:
# Objective

- `SystemStates` rock for dealing with exclusive world access, but are hard to figure out how to use.
- Fixes #3341.

## Solution

- Clearly document how to use `SystemState`, and why they're useful as an end-user.
pr_comments:
@TheRawMeatball, the caching example is rather involved (relevant to discussion in #3774).

I think I can get it working with a resource scope, but this pattern is clearly suboptimal.
Hm, resource_scope is how I do the caching usually, but given the boilerplate associated I agree we could make it better. I'd use resource_scope for now, and we can make a better API for this later.

>  Should there be a quick passage on why resource scope might be desirable in certain situations?

It's probably slightly faster in general, and can be clearer / less verbose. I don't think it's worth including without benchmarks that are outside of the scope of this PR.

issue_context.title: Document SystemState's use as an important tool for working with `World`
issue_context.body:
[SystemState](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/0bf90bb98db0b977a35d4fb39c06e9dca9bf7f04/crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/function_system.rs#L59) and particularly `SystemState::new` are incredibly powerful new tools for working directly with the world. Effectively, this allows you to extract data from the world as if you were running a system, properly handling conflicting accesses.

These deserve proper documentation, including a working example.

The basic pattern is to pass in your the types of your system parameters as a tuple into the generics of `SystemParam::new`, and then unpack the results into named arguments. If you're tackling this, feel free to ping me for more guidance.

review_comments: Very happy you added a reference in the world docs for discoverability!
